summary: The weighted tournament proof is now complete: complementarity makes expected total weight halve, a dominant vertex retains weight above one-half until selected, and Markov bounds its omission. Fresh comparison registers realize the product weights without estimating them; bounded amplification preserves the exact pivot law. A coupling charges only failures before the dominant vertex is selected, which avoids requiring a sampler guarantee on later tiny weights. The cyclic and fractional four-candidate examples usefully test the mechanism. The actual comparator canonically orders pairs and retains address labels, so its marginal law is a classical mixture with complementary orientations. Verification fixes a fresh measured address and searches exact failed tests; on zero inputs all addresses fail somewhere, and on one inputs the unique winner passes at its true address. The zero/one error bounds follow with fresh verifications.
